Triage: lands in the 401 producer behind `enforceAuth` in `packages/rest` ⇒ `domain:cli`; queued as Bug — the 401 family is the one error family whose body carries no `code` key, which already cost measurable ledger coverage (#9333's c0/c3 `partial`). Preferred direction: **add `code: "UNAUTHENTICATED"` alongside the existing keys** (additive, aligns the outlier family to the `{error, code}` shape the other six teach) rather than declaring the divergence in the ledger — declaring an exception would make every client carry a special case forever. **Clause-② flag: the fix touches a public wire shape** (adds a key to every 401 body) — claim declares `Clause-②: yes`, dispatch at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Pin the property the card names: one documented key identifies the code on every error family, 401 included. (Triage seat, session `session_019gCKd9EZfQ6MbGTnMHHJvW`.)

Container & model: `S–M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — tier derived this round from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`: **no path-derived mandate** (floor sonnet · default opus · ceiling fable), ⛔ not recalled.

**Clause-② and the downgrade, stated precisely.** Adding a `code` key to every 401 body changes the shape of a **published** error family. ⚠️ That is Clause-② territory judged from content, and it would ordinarily be fable-mandatory. This card is one of the **five the maintainer named in the one-time downgrade to `opus`** (#9446, #9416, #9462, #9488, #9487) — which is precisely why that authorisation exists. ⇒ `opus`, authorised, ⛔ does not spread beyond those five, ⛔ reverts to default when Fable recovers.

## Why this card and not #9488

#9488 and #9487 both land in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, so they are **hard serial against each other** — same file, and the maintainer's exemption explicitly kept same-file serialisation. Only one could go.

Under the lane's total order they tie at every level: both `pm:queue`, both type `Bug`, neither on a `target:` board, neither `pm:blocking`, neither `priority:p0`. The tie-break is **card age**, and it is uncomfortably fine:

- #9487 — created `2026-08-18T04:09:08Z`
- #9488 — created `2026-08-18T04:09:19Z`

**Eleven seconds.** I am taking #9487 because that is what the rule says, and stating the margin rather than dressing it up as a judgement — an eleven-second age gap is not a reason, it is a tie-breaker doing its job. #9488 goes next round, unless something outranks it by then. ⛔ It is **not** blocked and ⛔ not on hold; it is queued behind a same-file sibling.

## Premise check

⚠️ `rest-server.ts` took **three** landings today — #9426 (audit limb, `ed4ca5999`), #9454 (`/meta` read doors, `b6c769019`), and it is the same file #9488 waits on. Any line number in this card's body is stale by construction. The dispatch declares surface by **symbol and region** and instructs re-derivation on the current `main`.

Serial constraints cleared:
- **Same file** — `rest-server.ts` is clear as of `b6c769019`: #9454 merged (verified two readings plus probe `organizationIdForMetaRead`, 0 → 9 occurrences across 3 files). **#9488 is the one card still waiting on this file and is deliberately not dispatched.**
- **Same package** — parallel authoring permitted under the 2026-08-18 exemption; four replacement rules carried into the dispatch.
- Dispatched alongside **#9666** (`packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts`) — different package, different file, no read coupling.

## Returned to `needs-user-decision` — ⛔ this seat cannot rule it, and my own dispatch brief was self-contradictory

`domain:cli` seat, session `session_012WKSnqAaoqtW3QX7SSf1Vk`, PM loop round 20. Paired with the label write (`pm:dispatched` → `needs-user-decision`). Dev returned `status: needs_decision`, **no PR, zero commits** — it stopped rather than guessing, which is the correct outcome.

### ⛔ My error first: the two Zone 1 rulings I issued cannot both be satisfied

My brief said (①) converge onto the sibling ADR-0112 envelope, and (②) never weaken a gate. **On this family those are mutually exclusive**, and I did not know it when I wrote them.

I verified the mechanism myself rather than taking the report. `packages/core/src/security/anonymous-deny.ts`, in its **own doc comment**:

> *"Both shapes are pinned against a real booted showcase by `packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-anonymous-deny-surfaces.dogfood.test.ts`, which classifies every anonymous 401 into exactly one of the two families and **fails on a third dialect** or on a seam that changes family."*

⇒ For this family the nested envelope ① prescribes **is** the third dialect that classifier exists to reject. Landing it requires rewriting the classifier — the gate-weakening ② forbids. The dev measured the conflict and stopped; it did not pick the ruling it preferred.

### ⛔ My file surface was also wrong

I declared `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, "the 401-emitting auth-refusal region only". The body is **not local to that file**. It is `ANONYMOUS_DENY_BODY`, a constant at `packages/core/src/security/anonymous-deny.ts:85`, written verbatim at `rest-server.ts:1146` and reached from all **69** `enforceAuth` call sites. Confirmed on `origin/main`.

### The enumeration, and a refinement of the card's own title

Five 401 emission sites on current `main`, re-derived (⛔ not the card's stale line numbers):

| site | shape | `code` |
|---|---|---|
| `rest-server.ts:1146` `enforceAuth` | `ANONYMOUS_DENY_BODY` — flat, `error` is a **string** | ⛔ absent |
| `:4403`, `:4964` book/docs gates | `sendDeclaredFault` — flat `{ error: message, code }` | present, flat |
| `:8690`, `:8822` `/security/*` | `sendEnvelopeError` — nested | present, nested — already conformant |
